name: TaskFlow — the project you build
summary: One application, built across all sixteen phases. It starts as a console app that holds tasks in a list and ends as a containerised ASP.NET Core API with PostgreSQL, JWT authentication, layered architecture, a test suite and structured logging. You never throw the code away and start again — each stage refactors what you already wrote. You create it at ~/taskflow in Phase 0; the hub's project/starter-kit folder has the build configuration, compose file and scripts to copy in.

stages.title: Console task manager
stages.goal: Model the domain in C# and manipulate tasks in memory. No database, no web, no frameworks — just the language.
deliverables: TaskItem, Project, User, TaskStatus, Priority as records/classes/enums
An in-memory TaskStore with add, complete, delete and query operations
LINQ-powered filtering, grouping and reporting
Async simulated I/O with cancellation support

stages.title: A proper .NET solution
stages.goal: Turn a single file of code into a real solution with projects, packages, configuration and dependency injection.
deliverables: TaskFlow.sln with Domain, Application and Console projects
Directory.Build.props with shared settings
appsettings.json + environment variable configuration
Generic Host with DI and logging wired up

stages.title: REST API
stages.goal: Expose the domain over HTTP with correct status codes, DTOs, validation and OpenAPI docs.
deliverables: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/tasks with an in-memory store
Request and response DTOs separate from domain models
FluentValidation or DataAnnotations model validation
ProblemDetails error handling middleware and Swagger UI

stages.title: PostgreSQL + EF Core
stages.goal: Replace the in-memory store with a real relational database and migrations.
deliverables: TaskFlowDbContext with entity configurations
Users, Projects, Tasks, Comments, Labels and the many-to-many join
EF Core migrations applied to a Dockerised PostgreSQL
Pagination, filtering and search done in SQL, not in memory
stages.run: docker compose up -d db && dotnet ef database update

stages.title: Authentication and authorization
stages.goal: Let real users register, log in and only touch their own data.
deliverables: Registration with password hashing
JWT access tokens plus refresh tokens
Claims, roles and policy-based authorization
Ownership checks so a user cannot read another user's tasks

stages.title: Architecture clean-up
stages.goal: Restructure into layers you can justify, applying SOLID and only the patterns that earn their keep.
deliverables: Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api projects with enforced dependencies
Services behind interfaces, registered with the DI container
Mapping between entities and DTOs
A written note in the repo explaining each architectural trade-off

stages.title: Tests
stages.goal: Prove the behaviour, so you can refactor without fear.
deliverables: xUnit unit tests for domain rules and services
Mocked dependencies with NSubstitute
Integration tests using WebApplicationFactory
Database tests against a real PostgreSQL in Testcontainers

stages.title: Production ready
stages.goal: Make it something you would be comfortable deploying and operating.
deliverables: Structured logging, health checks, caching and rate limiting
Background service for notifications and audit history
Multi-stage Dockerfile and docker compose with PostgreSQL
Environment-based configuration and secret handling
